scenes.title: 1976 Surrey AV Studio: Covering the Monitor Screen Flips 'DA-DA' Instantly Back to 'BA-BA'
scenes.era: 1976, University of Surrey Audiovisual Psychology Suite, Guildford, UK

layout.description: Sunlit 1976 British university audiovisual control room with a crisp wooden-cabinet studio monitor displaying a close-up face pronouncing open-mouth 'GA-GA', a freestanding desktop loudspeaker cone beside acoustic waveform meters consistently reading 'BA-BA', and an opaque white occlusion paddle used to cover and uncover the screen.

positions.who: Harry McGurk (mannequin in 1976 British tweed jacket and wide-lapel shirt)
positions.where: holding a white cardstock screen-cover paddle inches in front of the studio monitor — pulling it aside ('98% Hear DA!') then sliding it back ('100% Hear BA!')
leaning toward the loudspeaker in disbelief as closing their eyes or blocking the screen switches what their ears hear on an unchanged audio loop

props.name: 1976 studio video monitor ('Visual Lips: GA') paired with desktop loudspeaker ('Audio Wave: BA')
props.period_detail: side-by-side display + speaker making the conflicting sensory inputs crystal clear

props.name: sliding white 'Eyes Open = DA / Screen Covered = BA' test paddle
props.period_detail: simple hand-held occlusion board blocking ONLY the visual face while the speaker cone plays unobstructed
props.physical_behavior: proves instantly that the sound room never changed the audio

actions.verb_sequence: plays the repeating 'BA' loudspeaker loop with the monitor uncovered -> Subject points confidently to the 'DA' response card -> McGurk slides the white paddle in front of the monitor screen without touching the speaker -> Subject gasps and points immediately to 'BA'

reactions.reaction: opens and closes hands over eyes repeatedly laughing as 'DA' and 'BA' flip back and forth
logs 98% adult fusion in the 1976 Nature data sheet

scenes.wardrobe: 1976 British academic attire: warm tweed jacket, patterned tie, collared shirt, knit jumper.
scenes.recognition_hook: Don't touch the volume knob — just cover the TV screen with a piece of cardboard and watch 'DA-DA' turn instantly into 'BA-BA'.

key_visual.description: a 1976 researcher in an audiovisual lab sliding a white paddle across a video monitor showing 'GA' lips beside a desktop loudspeaker playing 'BA' while a seated subject flips between 'DA' and 'BA' cards

scenes.title: 3-Year-Olds vs Adults: Growing Stronger Visual Lip Weighting

layout.description: Bright play-testing table where a 4-year-old and an adult listen to the same dubbed clip.

positions.where: comparing 59% child fusion vs 98% adult fusion as lip-reading experience matures

props.name: age-curve placard ('Age 3-4: 59% -> Adult: 98%')
props.period_detail: shows lifelong speech watching strengthens audiovisual coupling

actions.verb_sequence: tests child vs adult cohort across identical dub clips

reactions.reaction: plot developmental rise in visual speech influence

scenes.recognition_hook: Even four-year-olds fuse sight and sound — and by adulthood 98% of us let lips rewrite our ears.

scenes.title: 2010 TMS Proof: Switching Off the pSTS Mixing Board

layout.description: Clean bright neurophysiology room where a figure-eight TMS coil rests gently over the left posterior temporal scalp.

positions.where: delivering a single harmless magnetic pulse over left pSTS right as the 'BA+GA' clip plays
suddenly reporting the true acoustic 'BA' during pSTS disruption while seeing and hearing normally

props.name: handheld figure-eight TMS coil & pSTS target diagram
props.period_detail: temporarily uncouples visual lips from auditory speech

actions.verb_sequence: triggers brief pSTS pulse -> Volunteer taps 'BA' instead of 'DA'

reactions.reaction: amazed that 'DA' returns the next second without stimulation

scenes.wardrobe: Crisp white lab coat and casual shirt.
scenes.recognition_hook: Pause one thumbnail-sized patch in the temporal lobe for a tenth of a second, and the phantom 'DA' disappears.

scenes.title: The Free 15-Decibel Hearing Boost in Noisy Rooms

layout.description: Sunlit lively cafe where two friends turn chairs to face each other directly in clear window light.

positions.where: leaning in face-to-face effortlessly catching every word despite background espresso noise

props.name: well-lit face-to-face seating
props.period_detail: lets 120-ms visual lip lead prime auditory cortex

actions.verb_sequence: turns toward window light speaking clearly -> Friend B understands effortlessly without shouting

scenes.recognition_hook: Putting on your glasses in a loud restaurant genuinely helps you HEAR — because your temporal lobe lip-reads every syllable.
